rows.notes: SECONDARY CITATION, NO VALUES. Verbatim context: Chi et al. (2017) distinguished (a) 'a mild, transient and dose-dependent thrombocytopenia that is not necessarily involved in bleeding episodes' from (b) 'a marked thrombocytopenia, emerging after repeated exposure to AONs and resulting in multiple hemorrhages in monkeys. The latter was also found in clinical studies with other ASOs, e.g. drisapersen.' Graded 3 on the described severity ('marked thrombocytopenia ... multiple hemorrhages'), but EVERY quantitative field is TBD because this source reports no drisapersen numbers, dose, or study. Row retained only because the compound is explicitly named with an exact locus.

rows.notes: Verbatim: 'Age effects in the inotersen group in CS2 (disadvantaging subjects >=65 y) were more pronounced for the cardiac disorders SOC, Musculoskeletal and Connective Tissue Disorders SOC, chills, and platelet count decreased. These effects were not seen in the placebo group.' The tabulated age table on p104-107 does not break out a platelet row, so NO NUMERIC VALUE is available - readout_value TBD. Consequence: SmPC section 4.4 carries a warning that age >60 is a bleeding risk factor.

rows.source_table: p108, section 2.6 Clinical safety, 'Immunological events' (TEAEs by ADA status)
rows.notes: AESI thrombocytopenia (sum of thrombocytopenia + platelet count decreased) in ANTI-DRUG-antibody-positive subjects. Key negative: anti-inotersen ADA status did NOT stratify the platelet signal in CS2, mirroring the monkey finding that ADAs did not explain severe thrombocytopenia (p25). In CS3, however, platelet decreases >=30% and >=50% from baseline were more frequent in ADA-positive subjects (p109/p115).

rows.notes: Verbatim p109: 'Platelet decreases of >=30% and >=50% from baseline in CS3 were more frequently experienced by ADA positive subjects in both treatment groups.' p115 frames the same observation as 'supporting the hypothesis of an immunologically-mediated process'. NO NUMERIC VALUES are given for this stratification in the source, so readout_value is TBD. Note this CS3 finding is in tension with the CS2 ADA-status null result (23.5% vs 24.7%) recorded in the two rows above.

rows.notes: Verbatim: 'Treatment-emergent antiplatelet antibodies (IgG and IgM) and anti-PF4 antibodies (IgG, IgM, and IgA) were seen in subjects receiving inotersen (~29% of inotersen-treated in CS2 and >53% of subjects in CS3 [where all subjects received inotersen])'. rows.notes: Verbatim: 'No consistent effect on platelets was seen in the Phase 1 study with multiple dosing' (study CS1, healthy subjects). Dose band taken from the CS1 multiple-dose cohorts tabulated in Table 1, p31-32 (50, 100, 200, 300, 400 mg s.c.). Explicit grade-0 row in healthy volunteers - the platelet signal is patient/duration dependent, not seen in short-term Phase 1.

rows.notes: Adjacent-haematology context row (is_platelet_specific FALSE). Verbatim: 'Coagulation abnormalities as pre-defined by the Applicant (coagulation parameters, e.g. aPTT, INR, PT) did not constitute a safety issue in either study with similar incidences of respective TEAEs in subjects on inotersen and placebo.' Grade 0. Broader thrombotic SAEs (embolic stroke, PE, DVT, mesenteric artery occlusion) showed no increased incidence vs placebo either (3.6% vs 3.3%, p135 Effects Table). Verbatim: 'an initial rise in platelet values from baseline was observed in studies CS2 and CS3 upon initiation of inotersen treatment, i.e. at Week 2/3. rows.notes: Kinetics of the common decline: 'Decreases in the inotersen group occurred gradually over a period of several weeks, with an onset within the first 13 weeks of dosing and a mean nadir between 3 to 6 months after treatment initiation.' Graded 1 because it describes the mild/common pole; the value is a time, not a platelet count, so it carries no severity of its own. The actual nadir counts are in Fig. S11, which could not be retrieved.

rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Importantly, further investigation ruled out a heparin-induced thrombocytopenia-type mechanism and effects on platelet production'
rows.notes: MECHANISTIC NEGATIVE, and the most useful row in this paper for anyone modelling mechanism: the authors explicitly exclude both a HIT-type mechanism and a production/megakaryocyte defect, leaving peripheral antibody-mediated destruction. Grade 0 because no megakaryocyte or production abnormality was observed -- this is a genuine explicit no-effect finding at the stated locus, not an absence of mention. readout_value is TBD because the paper gives no assay, no numbers, and no supporting data for the exclusion; the claim is qualitative.

rows.exposure_duration: post-monitoring period of the 65wk dosing phase (not separately quantified)
rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'No cases of thrombocytopenia with platelet counts of less than 50,000 per cubic millimeter occurred after the institution of weekly platelet monitoring'
rows.notes: EXPLICIT ZERO, and it is evidence. Had events occurred in this band (<50x10^9/L) the row would have carried grade 3; it is recorded as grade 0 so the severe band stays findable. Important interpretation: this zero measures the effect of a risk-mitigation protocol (weekly platelet monitoring plus dose-stopping rules), not an absence of intrinsic hazard -- the same compound produced three <25x10^9/L events before monitoring was intensified. The denominator and duration of the post-monitoring period are not given in the main text, hence exposure_duration is qualitative.

rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Platelet counts in 2 of these 3 patients returned to baseline or near-baseline levels after discontinuation of the trial regimen and treatment with glucocorticoids. The third patient presented with an intracranial hemorrhage and died before treatment could be initiated'
rows.notes: recovered_after_discontinuation. Graded on the severity of the underlying event (<25x10^9/L, grade 3) -- reversibility does not downgrade an event that was life-threatening while it lasted, and one of the three did not recover. Glucocorticoid responsiveness is one of the two pieces of evidence the authors give for an immune-mediated mechanism (the other being anti-platelet IgG, next row).

rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'There was some evidence of an immune-mediated mechanism in the severe events, as indicated by recovery with glucocorticoid treatment and the presence of antiplatelet IgG in each of the 3 patients'
rows.notes: Anti-platelet IgG detected in all three patients with severe thrombocytopenia. Grade 3 is taken directly from the rubric clause 'immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with confirmed anti-platelet antibodies'. This row is the mechanistic core of the rare/severe/idiosyncratic pole of the bimodal endpoint and should not be collapsed with the mild count-decline rows. Assay, titre, and timing are not given in the main text.

rows.effect_vs_control: 3pct(3/112)_inotersen; no placebo case reported at this threshold
rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Thrombocytopenia with platelet counts of less than 25,000 per cubic millimeter occurred in 3 patients (3%) who received inotersen' (also stated in Discussion, paragraph 2)
rows.notes: THE CANONICAL SEVERE ANCHOR. <25x10^9/L is CTCAE grade 4 -> schema grade 3. Graded on the severity of the event, not on the smallness of the 3% incidence. One of the three patients died of intracranial haemorrhage. The paper does not tabulate a placebo figure at this threshold, so no explicit-zero control row is emitted for it (absence of a statement is not a grade-0 datum).

rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 3: 'Two patients in the inotersen group had a dose reduction to 150 mg weekly because of decreases in platelet counts'
rows.notes: GRADE 2 ANCHOR, and one of the few clean ones in the clinical literature for this endpoint: the rubric assigns grade 2 to a platelet decline 'requiring monitoring, dose interruption, or dose reduction', and this is an actioned dose reduction (300 -> 150 mg weekly) taken specifically for falling platelets. The platelet counts that triggered the reduction are not stated, so severity is inferred from the clinical action, which is precisely what the rubric asks for at this grade.

rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 4, final sentence: 'The incidence of hemorrhages was similar in the two groups'
rows.notes: GRADED 0, NOT 3, and this is the deliberate application of the schema's bleeding-attribution rule. An aggregate bleeding rate that is similar to placebo is a background rate, not a drug-induced platelet injury; grading it 3 on the word 'hemorrhage' would manufacture a severe event out of a null result. The one bleed that IS attributable to thrombocytopenia (the fatal intracranial haemorrhage) is captured on its own rows at grade 3. is_platelet_specific FALSE because this aggregate term is not platelet-attributed. No numerator or denominator is printed, hence readout_value TBD.

rows.effect_vs_control: at least 10pct incidence and at least 2x the placebo rate (magnitude given only in Table S11, not retrievable)
rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 4, term 'lowered platelet counts' in the same >=10% / >=2x-placebo sentence (citing Table S11)
rows.notes: The paper lists 'lowered platelet counts' as a term separate from 'thrombocytopenia' at the same locus, so it is carried as a separate row rather than merged. Numeric incidence unavailable (Table S11 not retrievable) -> TBD. Grade 1 for the same reason as the thrombocytopenia_incidence row: this is the common laboratory-decline pole, severity unstated here.

rows.effect_vs_control: at least 10pct incidence and at least 2x the placebo rate (magnitude given only in Table S11, not retrievable)
rows.source_table: Results, SAFETY, paragraph 4: 'Adverse events with both an incidence of at least 10% in either group and an incidence that was at least twice as high in the inotersen group as in the placebo group were nausea, pyrexia, chills, vomiting, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and lowered platelet counts (Table S11 ...)'
rows.notes: readout_value is TBD ON PURPOSE. The main text states only that thrombocytopenia met the >=10% / >=2x-placebo threshold; the numeric incidence sits in Table S11 of the Supplementary Appendix, which is paywalled at NEJM and reCAPTCHA-gated on the PMC supplement mirror. No number is invented here. Graded 1 as the common/mild pole -- severity is not stated at this locus, and the severe cases are captured by the dedicated <25x10^9/L, SAE, and fatal-haemorrhage rows. (For calibration only, not entered as a value: the FDA Tegsedi label Table 2 gives 24% vs 2% for this same trial.)

rows.source_table: Table 2 (Summary of Adverse Events), row 'Intracranial hemorrhage', inotersen column, with footnote sec-sign: 'The patient had a fatal intracranial hemorrhage that was associated with grade 4 thrombocytopenia'
rows.notes: Serious adverse event = intracranial haemorrhage, fatal, EXPLICITLY ATTRIBUTED by the table footnote to grade 4 thrombocytopenia. Grade 3 on attribution, exactly as the rubric requires -- not on the keyword 'hemorrhage'. The same patient appears in the Fig 1 legend among discontinuations for intracranial hemorrhage and in the Results narrative with a platelet count <10x10^9/L (separate row, distinct locus and readout).

rows.source_table: Table 2 (Summary of Adverse Events), row 'Intracranial hemorrhage', placebo column (N = 60)
rows.notes: PLACEBO ROW, dose_or_conc_value = 0. Explicit tabulated zero intracranial haemorrhages in the placebo arm; the comparator for the fatal thrombocytopenia-attributed bleed. Graded 0 on what was observed.

rows.source_table: Table 2 (Summary of Adverse Events), row 'Thrombocytopenia' under 'Any serious adverse event -> Event related to trial regimen', inotersen column
rows.notes: Serious, drug-related thrombocytopenia -> grade 3. INTERNAL DISCREPANCY WITHIN THE PAPER, flagged rather than smoothed: Table 2 lists 2 (2%), while the Abstract and Results state that thrombocytopenia was among 'the most frequent serious adverse events ... in 3 patients [3%]'. The two reconcile if the third severe case is the one Table 2 codes as 'Intracranial hemorrhage 1 (<1%)', whose footnote states it was associated with grade 4 thrombocytopenia. Curators joining on this row should not add 2 + 3.

rows.source_table: Table 2 (Summary of Adverse Events), row 'Thrombocytopenia', placebo column (N = 60)
rows.notes: PLACEBO ROW, dose_or_conc_value = 0. Explicit tabulated zero: no serious thrombocytopenia in 60 placebo patients over the same 65 weeks. Would have carried grade 3 had events occurred; recorded as grade 0 so the severe band and its denominator remain findable. This is the cleanest control comparator in the paper for the severe pole.
